description: The Bray and von Storch surveys of climate scientists, 1996-2015/16: the attribution and 'occurring now' questions and the model-process adequacy questions, read from the original reports on 2026-10-01/02. Counts for 2008 are reconstructed from the unlabelled histograms (bar heights measured in the rendered figure) and reproduce the reports' means and standard deviations exactly; 2013 and 2015/16 counts are from the figures' percentage labels (which are exact fractions of N).

sources.1996_2003: Bray & von Storch (2007) GKSS 2007/11, figures 1-6, 28, 30, 60 (hereon.de copy)
sources.2008: Bray & von Storch (2010) GKSS 2010/9 (CliSci2008), questions 10, 12a-f, 20-22 (hereon.de copy)
sources.2013: Bray & von Storch (2014) HZG Report 2014-4 (CliSci2013), questions 5-9, 26-28 (hereon.de copy)
sources.2015_16: Bray & von Storch (2016) HZG Report 2016-2, figures 1-21 (TIB edocs copy)

1996.question: Climate change is mostly the result of anthropogenic causes (1 strongly agree - 7 strongly disagree)

2008.question: How convinced are you that most of recent or near future climate change is, or will be, a result of anthropogenic causes? (1 not at all - 7 very much)
2008.note: counts reconstructed from the histogram; reproduce mean and sd exactly

2015_16_share.question: Since 1850 ... warmed by 0.5-0.7 C. Approximately what percent would you attribute to human causes? (1: 0%; 2: 1-25%; 3: 26-50%; 4: 51-75%; 5: 76-100%)

2013_confidence_in_AR4_attribution.question: Since the 2007 IPCC AR4 to now, do you feel more confident or less confident concerning the IPCC's attribution of warming to GHG? (1 much less - 4 no change - 7 much more)

1996.question: We can say for certain that global warming is a process already underway (1 strongly agree - 7 strongly disagree)

2008.question: How convinced are you that climate change, whether natural or anthropogenic, is occurring now? (1 not at all - 7 very much)
2008.note: counts reconstructed from the histogram; reproduce mean and sd exactly

model_processes_mean_1_very_inadequate_7.question: How well do you think atmospheric (climate) models can deal with ...

precipitation.note_2015_16: the report's Figure 7 histogram repeats the clouds bars; only the mean is usable

greenhouse_gases_knowledge_2015_16.question: The current state of scientific knowledge is developed well enough to allow for a reasonable estimate of the effects of greenhouse gases from anthropogenic sources on climate (1 not at all - 7 very much)

gcm_50yr_global_mean_temperature_2015_16.question: ability of global climate models to simulate a global mean value for temperature for the next 50 years (1 very poor - 7 very good)

attribution_of_extreme_events_2015_16.question: With how much certainty can we attribute recent extreme climate events to climate change (anthropogenic or otherwise)? (1 not at all - 7 very much)

value_neutral_mean_1_not_at_all_7_great_.question: To what degree do you think climate science has remained a value-neutral science?

uncertainty_since_1996.question: Since 1996 the level of uncertainty in climate science has (1 dropped considerably - 4 remained the same - 7 increased considerably)

distortion_for_political_arguments.question: As the values of non-scientists are taken into account, how much have scientific ideas been distorted to service political arguments concerning climate change? (1 not at all - 7 very much)

samples.1996: 500 hard copies in Germany, Denmark, Canada, USA (+ Italy, Taiwan); N about 540
samples.2008: three lists (top-10 ISI climate journals' authors; Oreskes 2004 list; institute mailing lists); 18 % response; N 370-373
samples.2013: 2008 list + ClimList + IPCC contributors; 4,491 valid addresses; 286 valid returns, 7 %
samples.2015_16: updated 2013 lists; 3,879 valid addresses; 651 returns, 17 %; mid-December 2015 to end of January 2016
